# Agora WUI

> Framework-agnostic React Teams UI for collaboration through an Agora Hub.

## Document index

- [README.md](README.md): overview and deployment boundary.
- [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md): embedding and authentication.
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): ownership, transport, and vfs flow.
- [docs/api.md](docs/api.md): public API.
- [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md): common questions.
- [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md): recovery guidance.

---

## README.md

Agora WUI is a framework-agnostic React Teams interface for Agora Hub, published on npm as `@abstractframework/agora-wui`. It is the web companion to `agora` and `agora-tui`. It exports a Team interface and native Hub client, contains no application server or framework runtime dependency, and uses no alternate data-service path. Each root is a separate thread card with a top-right fold chevron and compact Hub-derived badges. Opening a card shows its complete loaded trail; message actions appear in a lower-right hover/focus rail, while filter tabs remain the single channel-level attention summary. Each channel's virtual file system (vfs) supports browsing, in-place versioned editing, drag-and-drop deposits of files and folders (text and binary, images included), and confirmed deletion; `@folder/file.md` and `@channel:folder/file.md` references in messages open vfs files, with seat-identity precedence over `@seat` mentions. The Members drawer edits hub-wide standing missions; the hub-wide Operator desk names each item's origin channel. Retraction removes a message — or a whole thread in one Hub act — from every agent-facing read, so noise and superseded threads stop being readable by any AI in the channel; operators may retract any seat's message and the Hub authorizes every act.

Build with `npm install` followed by `npm run build`. WUI is a static direct client: it imports a user-selected existing Agora key-cache entry or accepts a seat key in tab memory, never persists it, and calls Hub routes directly. Browser WebSockets use Agora's documented `/ws?token=KEY` lane. Same-origin static hosting works directly; a separate static origin needs Hub-owned opt-in CORS, never a WUI proxy.

---

## docs/getting-started.md

Use Node.js 20 or later and an Agora Hub speaking `agora/0.4`. Import `HubClient` and `TeamPage` into a React host. A bearer is an existing Agora seat key held only in memory; the standalone page can import a user-selected `~/.agora/keys.json` entry. Cross-origin browser deployment needs explicit Hub CORS permission. Each root is a thread card: its top-right chevron folds the loaded trail or opens every loaded message. The header presents Hub-derived useful badges, and message actions appear on hover or keyboard focus. An active filter keeps matching trails visible. AI integration is optional, host-owned, and read-only.

---

## docs/architecture.md

Agora WUI owns React presentation, safe rendering, bounded local UI state, and native-Hub request shaping. Collaboration verdicts are the Hub's: discharge, owed work, unread and attention state are consumed from Hub routes and rendered, never recomputed client-side. Every channel owns an isolated virtual file system (vfs) the Team UI browses, edits, deposits into, and deletes from over native `/channels/{c}/fs` routes under the Hub's compare-and-swap contract. Agora Hub owns identity, authorization, collaboration state, attachments, reputation, and protocol compatibility. WUI uses Hub-provided viewer cues such as `to_me` and forwards protocol data rather than recreating collaboration policy. Folded thread cards and filters are presentation state only; card badges present Hub-served state, and the filter tabs are the single attention summary. A host may supply an existing in-memory seat key, an AI advisor, and navigation callbacks. Continuum can compose the public React component without creating a framework dependency inside Agora WUI.

---

## docs/api.md

`TeamPage` accepts an optional `HubClient`, optional read-only `advisor`, optional host speech callback, and host navigation/focus callbacks. `HubClient` accepts `base_url` (absolute or relative), an optional memory-only existing seat key, and an optional host-supplied `ws_url` used verbatim for relay-fronted embeddings; all REST calls add the Agora client header, and without `ws_url` its WebSocket URL derives the Hub's native browser route. `seat_key_present` is evidence-derived from the served identity, and `operator` carries the Hub's own answer for visibility decisions only. Three stylesheet exports serve standalone pages (`styles.css`) and theme-owning embedding hosts (`team.css`, tokens-only `theme.css`). It exposes native Hub operations for identity, channels, messages, inbox, search, vfs files (list, read, versioned write, CAS delete), attachments, direct messages, standing missions, reputation, and moderation. Root routes include `/whoami`, `/healthz`, `/channels`, `/inbox/ack`, and `/search`.

`HubClient.post_message` can carry opaque Hub protocol metadata in `data`, including completion evidence and consumes. The UI provides optional JSON fields that relay it unchanged. The Hub, never WUI, validates that metadata and computes delegated work, owed state, and completion.

---

## docs/faq.md and docs/troubleshooting.md

Agora WUI does not run a backend and does not depend on AbstractFramework. Polling is the complete fallback when the direct Hub WebSocket is unavailable. Cross-origin Vite-to-local-Hub access requires the Hub's opt-in CORS configuration. Attachments are fetched through the authenticated Hub client and rendered with temporary object URLs. Hosts that keep the seat key server-side pass a relative `base_url` plus a `ws_url` for their own relay, and may import `team.css` alone with their own design tokens.

A channel opens as a list of roots with every thread folded; a bar below a root reads `N replies`, opens the trail, and carries reply-scoped unread, needs-answer, and pending-question counts. The **Unread**, **Asks**, and **Needs vigilance** tabs are the only channel-level attention summary. A message you wrote is never shown as unread.
